blocks.text: Places, things and results
-ник — the place where the base's object lives, its territory
«место обитания, территория объекта, указанного в основе» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of -ник. Its examples: муравейник, коровник, крапивник, орешник.
Russian Wiktionary, «-ник», meaning 2 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ник).
-ищ — a place marked by the action of the base verb

««место, характеризующееся действием, которое названо мотивирующим глаголом»» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of -ищ. Its examples: прибежище, токовище, убежище, сборище, скопище, торжище.

blocks.text: Russian Wiktionary, «-ищ», meaning 2 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ищ).
-ок — (productive suffix, colloquial, unstressed, takes verbs, produces nouns) an object that remains after process is done

(productive suffix, colloquial, unstressed, takes verbs, produces nouns) an object that remains after process is done — обре́зать (“to clip, to trim”) + -ок → обре́зок (“clipping”); объесть (“to eat away”) + -ок → объе́док (“scrap”); о- + кури́ть (“to smoke”) + -ок → оку́рок (“butt”)
Wiktionary, «-ок» (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ок#Russian).
-ец — the result of the activity of the base
«результата указанной в основе деятельности» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of -ец. Its examples: рубец.
Russian Wiktionary, «-ец», meaning 5 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ец).
-ка — (added to verbs, forms abstract nouns or nouns indicating the result of the action)

(added to verbs, forms abstract nouns or nouns indicating the result of the action) — закали́ть (“to temper, to harden”) + -ка → зака́лка (“tempering, hardening; training (for endurance)”); мочи́ть (“to soak, to wet”) + -ка → мо́чка (“soaking, wetting”); отде́лать (“to finish, to trim”) + -ка → отде́лка (“finishing, trimming; finish, trim”)

-ина — suffix appended to nouns or adjectives to form a noun denoting a kind of meat
suffix appended to nouns or adjectives to form a noun denoting a kind of meat — бара́н (“ram, sheep”) + -ина → бара́нина (“mutton, lamb”); свинья́ (“pig, hog”) + -ина → свини́на (“pork”)
Wiktionary, «-ина» (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ина#Russian).
-ин — the meat of these animals
««мясо этих животных»» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of -ин. Its examples: баранина, лососина.
Russian Wiktionary, «-ин», meaning 2 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ин).
